To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Laplacian self-induced pressure is the source of wave dispersion and the origin of the irregular signals.

(i) the Laplacian self-induced pressure is responsible for wave dispersion and (ii) the Laplacians of the velocity components in the intermediate (adjustable) sublayer are responsible for wave dispersion.
the transition to turbulence is characterized by the emergence of solitarylike waves and that the phase speed of these waves exceeds the speed at which the weaker disturbances travel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism for the generation of irregular signals and coherent structures in transitional boundary layers.
a new type of solitary waves that may be excited in a boundary layer in transition to turbulence.
the generation of irregular oscillations and large-sized coherent waves in the boundary layer transitioning from laminar to turbulent regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the large-scale structures in transitional boundary layers are the outcome of a nonlinear mechanism that is independent of the Reynolds number.
the erratic oscillations are not a mere by-product of transition but a fundamental ingredient of the phenomenon.
the large-sized coherent structures are not generated by the erratic signals but are born independently of the small disturbances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present approach to the generation of irregular signals and solitarylike waves in boundary layers is a natural extension of the classical triple-deck model.
the transition process is not a continuous one, but is rather a sequence of discrete events.
the erratic signals are generated in the transitional boundary layer by the same mechanism as the large-sized waves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the erratic signals and solitarylike coherent structures are not independent but are interrelated.
the transition from a laminar flow to a fully developed turbulent flow can be regarded as the process of a gradual emergence of solitarylike waves from a foam of erratic signals.
the erratic signals and solitarylike waves are not mutually exclusive but are interrelated and can coexist in transitional boundary layers.
